newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil narrowly softer in slow start to week.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil narrowly softer in slow start to week.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil was a touch softer on Monday amid a quiet start to the week.

High sulphur barges were knocked lower in the morning with refinery material trading down up to $2 at $113 and $112 fob a tonne and went quiet in the afternoon. Traders said there was a lack of offered material which combined with poor physical bunker demand effectively dampened the whole sector.

High sulphur cracked cargoes also faced a sluggish day with end-user buying interest so discreet as to pressure prices very slightly. Russian straight run material was still available despite expectations of a fuel ban in the near future.
"Its very quiet at the moment, there's not much material, but buyers are also quiet," said one trader. Prices were assessed close to swaps at around $113-114 cif NWE.

Low sulphur cracked cargoes were easier amid a lack of interest for the larger lots. Offers from NWE were heard below $130 into Italy. One trader at a major estimated upwards of 150,000 tonnes was homeless up to the second decade of November suggesting further weakness. The Turkish tender to buy 55-60,000 tonnes of low sulphur was won by a trader, but gave little support to a well supplied sector, dealers said.
